stimulus.text: Two engravings from Theodor de Bry's America series (1591), after drawings by Jacques Le Moyne de Morgues. The first shows Florida Indians planting seeds of beans and maize in cleared fields. The second shows the same people hunting deer disguised under deerskins. De Bry never visited North America; he engraved the scenes in Europe from watercolors painted by Jacques Le Moyne, a French artist with the Laudonnière expedition.
stimulus.source_note: Engravings from the shared image pool; Theodor de Bry (1591), after Jacques Le Moyne de Morgues, public domain (Library of Congress).

stem: De Bry published these engravings in books sold to readers across Europe. How does that purpose and audience shape what the engravings show?

options.text: De Bry drew only what he had measured himself in Florida villages.
De Bry shaped the scenes to interest European readers buying his books.
De Bry printed the engravings to teach Native peoples European farming methods.
De Bry made the images as legal records for a Spanish colonial court.

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
